metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; adjust downward by 5–10% for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; apply a “mean-reversion” bias: anchor forecast to 30-day moving average of past 10 days.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; add a “trend decay” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for 5+ consecutive days of declining prices.
- For long-term (30-day) forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply a “smoothed horizon” rule: use 60-day moving average as baseline for 15+ day forecasts, unless sentiment indicates strong directional bias.
- If sentiment history is non-zero (even if small), model should adjust forecast toward sentiment direction; if sentiment > 0.1, add 2–5% to forecast; if sentiment < -0.1, subtract 2–5%.
